items.briefing:
Scammers are now hiding phishing attacks inside calendar invite files (.ics), which can appear in your inbox as a meeting request. If you accept or even open these, you may be directed to a malicious website or prompted to enter your credentials. This is a reminder to be cautious with unexpected calendar invites, especially from unknown senders or with vague subject lines.

**Practical tip:** Before accepting any calendar invite, check who sent it and whether you were expecting it — if in doubt, contact the sender directly through a separate channel to verify.
